incident-bot: PAGER TRIGGERED — P1 embeddings-queue-high-latency (INC-2028)
Details: embeddings-processor queue latency > 3s p95 for multiple customers. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2028 • Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-queue

Maya Patel: ACK — I'm on primary. pulling logs and metrics now.

Samir Rao: i'm joining as secondary. quick ask — customer impact?

Maya Patel: quick summary: 4 customers seeing sustained embedding latency 3-12s, error rate ~0% (no 5xx), just huge queueing. SLO breach for embeddings p95. We've scaled embeddings-processor and restarted workers. Root cause looks like redis evictions/timeouts on the vector cache.

Ena Li: tagging infra — redis cluster rdb-primary showing high CPU & evictions. @ops-bot can you post current redis metrics?

ops-bot: redis cluster rdb-primary (10.1.2.3) — CPU 98%, memory 92%, evictions 1200/s, rejected connections 0.5%. Last restart: 6d.

Tony Nguyen: i'll take redis. SSHing to rdb-primary, starting graceful restart of rdb-node-3.

Maya Patel: Mitigations applied so far:
- scaled embeddings-processor deployment from 3 -> 8 replicas
- disabled large batching in runtime (temp)
- restarted embeddings-worker pods (rolling)
Commands run:
```bash
kubectl scale deploy embeddings-processor --replicas=8 -n inference
kubectl rollout restart deploy/embeddings-worker -n inference
```
Result: queue length dropped ~40% in 4m, p95 improved from ~9s -> ~3.4s but still above SLO. Redis evictions still high.

Samir Rao: Customer impact details I have:
- cust-A & cust-B: p95 5-10s, intermittently timing out on side that enqueues (retries succeed)
- cust-C: degraded throughput, queued jobs growing earlier but draining now
Support notified: support-bot posted customer-facing advisory (no data loss).

support-bot: Notified Support & CSMs: "We're investigating increased embeddings latency affecting a small set of customers. No data loss. We'll update in 30m." :warning:

Tony Nguyen: Redis action log: did a rolling restart on rdb-node-3, reclaimed memory, evictions dropped to ~50/s, CPU down to 65%. Restart command used: `sudo systemctl restart redis` then `redis-cli INFO memory` to verify. Backlog now draining.

Maya Patel: good — that aligns with metrics. Next mitigation if evictions return: add an extra redis replica, or failover to secondary cluster (requires infra approval). Also consider enabling soft-limits on heavy customers (rate-limit embeddings per-min).

Samir Rao: For handoff — here's what to watch:
- embeddings queue length (Grafana: /d/embeddings/queue) — target <200
- redis evictions per-sec (Grafana: /d/infra/redis) — target 0-5/s
- p95 embeddings latency (API) — target <2s
- DLQ size and error logs: `kubectl logs -l app=embeddings-worker -n inference --since=30m | grep ERROR`
If latency creeps back up: revert batching change, scale processors further, or route heavy customers to `m-infer-lite`.

Maya Patel: Support message template we sent:
"We're currently mitigating increased embeddings latency. We've applied scaling and restarted infrastructure; performance is returning to normal. We'll monitor for 1 hour and follow up with details."

Tony Nguyen: verify infra notes — I updated runbook snippet with commands to add a redis replica and to perform controlled failover: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-queue#redis-failover
